issues.legal_issue: A later application to set aside an execution sale under the deposit procedure may be made and prosecuted after an earlier application to set aside the sale on other grounds is withdrawn, and is treated as made upon that withdrawal.
material_facts: In execution of a decree, the applicant first sought to set aside the sale under the procedure for challenging a sale on other grounds.
The applicant later filed an application under the deposit procedure, deposited the required amount, and stated in that application that the earlier application was withdrawn.
The court formally dismissed the earlier application only after the later application had been filed.
issues.conclusion: The later application was maintainable and was treated as made when the earlier application was withdrawn; the absence of a formal dismissal order at that point did not invalidate it.
issues.legal_principle: Order 21 Rule 89(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, gives effect to both the words “make” and “prosecute”: a person who first applies under Rule 90 cannot make or prosecute an application under Rule 89 unless the earlier application is withdrawn, and an application under Rule 89 made before that withdrawal is treated as made upon withdrawal. The interpretation is supported by the corresponding proviso to section 310A of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1882, and Rajendra Nath Haldar v. Nilratan Mitter, ILR 23 Calcutta 958, which construed “make” in that proviso to include carrying on or prosecuting an application.

rule.if: execution_sale_challenge and earlier_sale_challenge_filed and later_deposit_application_filed and earlier_application_withdrawn

predicates.execution_sale_challenge: The proceeding concerns an application to set aside a sale made in execution of a decree.
predicates.earlier_sale_challenge_filed: The applicant first filed an application to set aside the execution sale on grounds other than compliance with the deposit procedure.
predicates.later_deposit_application_filed: The applicant later filed an application relying on the deposit procedure to set aside the execution sale.
predicates.earlier_application_withdrawn: The applicant communicated withdrawal of the earlier sale-challenge application.

issues.definition: When an applicant in an execution-sale challenge first files one sale-challenge application, later files a deposit-based application, and withdraws the earlier application, the later application is treated as made upon that withdrawal.

issues.legal_issue: An applicant’s unconditional communication to the court that an application is withdrawn completes the withdrawal without requiring a court order permitting or recording it.
material_facts: The applicant stated in the later application that the earlier sale-challenge application was withdrawn and also filed a separate application stating that it did not wish to pursue the earlier application.
The court initially continued to take procedural steps in the earlier application and formally dismissed it only after the applicant again stated that it did not wish to prosecute it.
issues.conclusion: The earlier application was effectively withdrawn when the applicant communicated the withdrawal; the later formal dismissal merely recorded that withdrawal, and the intervening procedural steps did not undo it.
issues.legal_principle: A litigant has the right unconditionally to withdraw an application, and the withdrawal is effective upon communicating it to the court. No order permitting withdrawal is necessary; a formal order may simply record the withdrawal. The court applied this principle in interpreting Order 21 Rule 89(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

predicates.execution_sale_challenge: The proceeding concerns an application to set aside a sale made in execution of a decree.
predicates.applicant_unequivocally_notified_court_o: The applicant clearly informed the court that the applicant was withdrawing the application.

issues.definition: When an applicant in an execution-sale challenge clearly informs the court of withdrawal, the withdrawal takes effect upon that communication.
